title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving health service to the most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas in Diinsoor district of Bay region.

description.narrative: ltpgtDecades of conflict, disease outbreaks, widespread poverty, and recurrent climatic shocks, including the ongoing drought emergency, have devastated Somalia. New-Ways is proposing a 12-month integrated Health project targeting the most affected vulnerable populations in Diinsoor district, reaching a total of 50,000 persons, including 20,000 women, 5600 Men, 12,400 girls, and 12,000 boys. The proposed project will support 2 health facilities and 2 mobile centers in the Diinsoor district with an approximated population of 100,426. New-Ways plans to deliver an integrated package of promotive, preventive, and curative maternal, newborn child health services and scale-up outbreak early warning and response and case management of epidemic-prone diseases through 2 static health facilities and 2 mobile response team i.e Static health facilities (Waaberi -Ahmedgurey and Howlwadag-Kacaan while the mobile sites are (Mobile 1 (Qodqod IDP, Ramadhoway IDP and Yaaqshiq IDP) Mobile 2 (Korkamari IDP,Jilalow IDP and Buulifuur IDP) as part of the efforts to support the drought-affected communities in Diinsoor. The mobile clinics will be working every day except on Friday going to 3 IDPs per mobile twice a week. The project aims to scale up the static and mobile clinics in Diinsoor IDP and host community sites, and scale up the health care through skilled health professionals. New-Ways through this project will provide regular medical supplies and life-saving drugs to established health facilities, establish referral mechanisms and improve the coverage of measles vaccinations, and support safe motherhood and reproductive health while also ensuring readiness to prevent and respond to outbreaks such as malaria, measles or AWD/Cholera and promote health update through health education and beneficiary sensitization including management of rape and GBV. The project will engage the PLWD, minority groups and women and girls by ensuring representation, allowing access, direct engagement, collaborating, training, and engaging them as staff and beneficiariesltbrgtThe activities to be undertaken will include:ltbrgtProvision of Outpatient consultations to drought-affected IDPs in Diinsoor districtltbrgtProvision of routine and campaign immunization to children under 5 and TT to Women of childbearing age (WBCA)ltbrgtEnsure the treatment of common diseases such as pneumonia, diarrhea/dehydration, malaria, and skin conditionsltbrgtProvide antenatal and post-natal care to pregnant and lactating mothers at the 2 health facilities and the 2 Mobile sites.ltbrgtProvision of 24/7 delivery services in the two static health facilitylt/pgtltpgtConduct a community mobilization and awareness-raising workshop at the start of the project for 100 peopleltbrgtProcure Medical supplies and ensure that the 2 facilities have enough supplies throughout the project period.ltbrgtProvision of quality multi-sectoral services (clinical case management, PSS, justice, safetyltbrgtConduct quarterly supervision every 3 months for four quarters.ltbrgtlt/pgt
